mock_data.title: Too Much Traffic
mock_data.passage:
Many of the problems which face governments nowadays are international ones. Take traffic, for example. All the major cities of the world are having to try to find ways of dealing with too many vehicles and the congested roads which they cause.

A large number of the vehicles which clog our cities are private cars. Motorists are very reluctant to leave their precious cars behind and go to work on public transport, despite the constant traffic jams. They regard buses, trams and trains as being for other people, while they themselves like to drive from door to door. Thus, our roads are chock-a-block with traffic.

Of course, parking space is not always available. Some firms provide car parks or garages, where at least some of their employees can leave their cars. Most people, however, have to rely on public car parks, often multi-storey ones, or else try to park in the street. Since this is usually highly restricted, with many parking meters in evidence, parking is a source of frustration to many motorists.

People who are otherwise quite law-abiding are apt to take a bit of a risk when it comes to traffic offences. Thus, they ignore both signs that say 'NO PARKING' and lines painted down the edge of the road which indicate parking restrictions. Should they be away from their cars for longer than the amount of time allowed by the parking meter, they are not worried—until they see that the traffic warden has left a parking ticket on their windscreen, and realize that they will have to pay a fine.

The authorities in more and more cities are trying to keep cars out of the city centre. With this aim, they have pedestrianized large areas and introduced park-and-ride schemes so that people will leave their cars at the city boundary and complete their journey by bus.

Still, there are fears that ever-increasing traffic will cause gridlock in cities, particularly at rush hours. With so many tailbacks and bottle-necks on so many roads, motoring is no longer a pleasure. Why, then, do so many of us persist in using our cars?

If they stay away from their cars for too long, they don't worry – until they see a parking ticket on their car window. Then they know they have to pay a fine.

mock_data.passageB2:
Many of the challenges facing governments today are global in nature. A prime example is traffic congestion. Major cities worldwide are struggling to devise solutions for the ever-increasing number of vehicles and the resulting road congestion. This issue demands attention and innovative strategies.

A significant contributor to urban traffic is the prevalence of private cars. Despite persistent traffic jams, many drivers are hesitant to abandon their vehicles and opt for public transportation. They often view buses, trams, and trains as alternatives for others, preferring the convenience of door-to-door driving. Consequently, our roads are frequently gridlocked with traffic.

Naturally, finding parking can be a challenge. While some companies provide parking facilities for their employees, most people must rely on public car parks, often multi-story structures, or attempt to park on the street. Given the often stringent restrictions and abundance of parking meters, finding a space becomes a source of frustration for many drivers. This situation often leads to stress and wasted time.

Otherwise law-abiding citizens sometimes take liberties when it comes to traffic regulations. They may disregard 'NO PARKING' signs or painted lines indicating parking restrictions. Even if they exceed the time limit on a parking meter, they might not worry – until they find a parking ticket on their windshield and realize they face a fine. This behavior highlights the temptation to bend the rules when convenience is at stake.

To address this, authorities in numerous cities are attempting to discourage car use in city centers. They have pedestrianized large areas and implemented park-and-ride schemes, encouraging people to leave their cars on the city outskirts and complete their journey by bus. These measures aim to reduce traffic volume in the most congested areas.

Despite these efforts, there are concerns that escalating traffic levels will cause complete standstills in cities, especially during rush hour. With frequent tailbacks and bottlenecks on numerous roads, driving is no longer an enjoyable experience. This raises the question: why do so many of us persist in using our cars, even when faced with these inconveniences? Perhaps it's time to re-evaluate our reliance on personal vehicles and explore alternative modes of transportation.
mock_data.passageC1:
The multifaceted challenges confronting contemporary governments are increasingly transnational in nature. Take, for instance, the pervasive issue of traffic congestion. Virtually all major urban centres globally are grappling with the imperative to devise effective strategies for managing the proliferation of vehicles and the resultant gridlock that chokes their road networks.

A significant proportion of the vehicles that inundate our cities are, undeniably, private automobiles. Motorists, it seems, are remarkably averse to abandoning the perceived comfort and convenience of their personal vehicles in favour of public transport, notwithstanding the persistent traffic bottlenecks. They often relegate buses, trams, and trains to the realm of alternative transportation for others, while simultaneously insisting on the door-to-door convenience afforded by private car ownership. This entrenched attitude contributes significantly to the saturation of our roadways.

Naturally, the availability of parking is not always guaranteed. While some organizations furnish car parks or garages, thereby accommodating at least a segment of their workforce, the majority of individuals are compelled to rely on public car parks, frequently multi-storey facilities, or alternatively, to attempt on-street parking. Given the prevalence of stringent regulations, often manifested in the ubiquitous presence of parking meters, securing a parking space constitutes a frequent source of exasperation for many drivers. The scarcity of parking leads to frustration and illegal parking.

Individuals who, under normal circumstances, adhere to legal and ethical standards are occasionally inclined to circumvent traffic regulations. Consequently, they may disregard 'NO PARKING' signs or painted road markings that delineate parking restrictions. Should their absence from their vehicles exceed the allotted time stipulated by the parking meter, they remain unconcerned – at least until the unwelcome sight of a parking ticket affixed to their windscreen dawns on them, forcing the realization that a fine will be levied. This is a common predicament for urban drivers.

Authorities in an increasing number of cities are actively pursuing measures to curtail vehicular access to city centres. To this end, they have implemented extensive pedestrianization schemes and introduced park-and-ride initiatives, with the objective of incentivizing individuals to leave their cars at the city's periphery and complete their journeys via public transportation. These are all attempts to alleviate congestion.

Nevertheless, there are persistent apprehensions that the relentless escalation of traffic volume will ultimately precipitate gridlock in urban areas, particularly during peak hours. With the pervasive presence of tailbacks and bottlenecks on a multitude of roads, the act of driving has devolved from a pleasurable experience into a frustrating ordeal. The question then arises: why do so many of us continue to perpetuate the use of our cars, despite these evident drawbacks?

mock_data.translation:
Hozirgi vaqtda hukumatlar duch kelayotgan ko'plab muammolar xalqaro xarakterga ega. Masalan, yo'l harakatini olaylik. Dunyoning barcha yirik shaharlari juda ko'p sonli transport vositalari va ular sabab bo'ladigan tirband yo'llar muammosini hal qilish yo'llarini topishga majbur bo'lmoqdalar.

Shaharlarimizni to'ldirib yuboradigan transport vositalarining katta qismi shaxsiy avtomobillardir. Haydovchilar doimiy tirbandliklarga qaramay, o'zlarining qadrli avtomobillarini qoldirib, ishga jamoat transportida borishni juda xohlamaydilar. Ular avtobus, tramvay va poyezdlarni boshqalar uchun deb hisoblaydilar, o'zlari esa eshikdan eshikkacha hayrashni yoqtiradilar. Shunday qilib, yo'llarimiz transport bilan liq to'la.

Albatta, to'xtash joyi har doim ham mavjud emas. Ba'zi firmalar kamida ba'zi xodimlari o'z mashinalarini qoldirishi mumkin bo'lgan avtoturargohlar yoki garajlar bilan ta'minlaydi. Biroq, aksariyat odamlar ochiq avtoturargohlarga, ko'pincha ko'p qavatli binolarga tayanishga yoki ko'chada to'xtashga harakat qilishga majbur bo'lishadi. Bu odatda qat'iy cheklangan bo'lganligi va ko'plab to'xtash hisoblagichlari mavjudligi sababli, to'xtash joyi ko'plab haydovchilar uchun norozilik manbai hisoblanadi.

Boshqa hollarda qonunga bo'ysunadigan odamlar yo'l harakati qoidalarini buzishga kelganda biroz tavakkal qilishga moyil bo'ladilar. Shunday qilib, ular 'TO'XTASH TAQIQLANGAN' belgilarini ham, yo'l chetidagi to'xtash cheklovlarini ko'rsatuvchi chiziqlarni ham e'tiborsiz qoldiradilar. Agar ular mashinalaridan to'xtash hisoblagichi tomonidan ruxsat etilgan vaqtdan uzoqroq vaqt davomida uzoqda bo'lishsa, ular tashvishlanmaydilar - to yo'l nazoratchisi old oynaga jarima kvitansiyasini qoldirganini ko'rmaguncha va jarima to'lashlari kerakligini tushunmaguncha.

Yana va yana ko'p shaharlardagi ma'murlar mashinalarni shahar markazidan uzoqlashtirishga harakat qilmoqdalar. Ushbu maqsad bilan ular katta maydonlarni piyodalar hududiga aylantirdilar va odamlar o'z mashinalarini shahar chegarasida qoldirib, sayohatlarini avtobusda yakunlashlari uchun "to'xtat va ket" (park-and-ride) sxemalarini joriy qildilar.

Shunga qaramay, tobora ortib borayotgan transport vositalari shaharlarda, ayniqsa tig'iz vaqtlarda to'liq to'xtab qolishga (gridlock) olib kelishi mumkin degan xavotirlar mavjud. Shunchalik ko'p navbatlar va tor joylar (bottle-necks) mavjud bo'lgan yo'llarda avtomobil haydash endi zavq bag'ishlamaydi. Unda nima uchun ko'pchiligimiz avtomobillardan foydalanishda davom etmoqdamiz?

gridlock.definition: A situation where roads in a town or city become so blocked with traffic that nothing can move.

mock_data.translationB1:
Hukumatlar bugungi kunda hal qilishga majbur bo'lgan ko'plab muammolar xalqaro xarakterga ega. Masalan, transport harakati haqida o'ylab ko'ring. Dunyo bo'ylab katta shaharlar juda ko'p mashinalar va ularning sabab bo'layotgan tirbandliklariga qarshi kurashish yo'llarini topishga harakat qilmoqda.

Shaharlarimizni to'ldirayotgan mashinalarning ko'pchiligi shaxsiy mashinalardir. Odamlar mashinalarini tashlab ketishni va jamoat transportidan foydalanishni xohlamaydilar, hatto tirbandliklar bo'lganda ham. Ular avtobus va poyezdlarni boshqa odamlar uchun deb o'ylashadi. Ular eshikdan eshikkacha haydashni yoqtirishadi. Shuning uchun yo'llarimiz transport harakati bilan to'lib-toshgan.

Albatta, to'xtash joyini topish har doim ham oson emas. Ba'zi kompaniyalarda o'z ishchilari uchun avtoturargohlar mavjud. Ammo ko'pchilik odamlar jamoat avtoturargohlaridan foydalanishlari yoki ko'chada to'xtashga harakat qilishlari kerak. Ko'pincha ko'plab to'xtash o'lchagichlari mavjud, shuning uchun to'xtash haydovchilar uchun asabiylashuvchi bo'lishi mumkin.

Odatda qonunga itoat qiladigan odamlar ba'zan transport harakati bilan bog'liq xavf-xatarlarga duch kelishadi. Ular 'TO'XTASH TAQIQLANADI' belgilari va yo'ldagi to'xtash qoidalarini ko'rsatadigan chiziqlarga e'tibor bermaydilar. Agar ular mashinalaridan uzoqda juda uzoq vaqt qolishsa, xavotirlanishmaydi - to mashina oynasida jarima talonini ko'rishmaguncha. Keyin ular jarima to'lashlari kerakligini bilishadi.

Borgan sari ko'proq shaharlar mashinalarni shahar markazidan uzoqroq tutishga harakat qilmoqda. Ular ba'zi hududlarni piyodalar zonasiga aylantirdilar, bu faqat odamlar u erda yurishi mumkin degan ma'noni anglatadi. Ular, shuningdek, odamlar o'z mashinalarini shahar tashqarisida qoldirib, avtobusda kirishi uchun "to'xtab-haydash" sxemalarini boshladilar.

Shunga qaramay, odamlar transport harakati ko'payib, shaharlarda, ayniqsa tiqilinch soatlarida to'liq tiqilishni keltirib chiqarishidan xavotirda. Yo'llarda shunchalik ko'p uzun navbatlar va tor joylar borki, haydash endi qiziqarli emas. Xo'sh, nega ko'pchiligimiz hali ham mashinalarimizdan foydalanamiz?

Bugungi kunda hukumatlar duch kelayotgan ko'plab muammolar global xarakterga ega. Bunga yaqqol misol - tirbandlik. Dunyo bo'ylab yirik shaharlar avtomobillar sonining doimiy ravishda ortib borishi va natijada yo'llarda tirbandlik yuzaga kelishi uchun yechimlar ishlab chiqishga urinmoqda. Bu masala e'tiborni va innovatsion strategiyalarni talab qiladi.

Shahar tirbandligiga katta hissa qo'shadigan omil - xususiy avtomobillarning keng tarqalganligi. Doimiy tirbandliklarga qaramay, ko'plab haydovchilar o'z avtomobillaridan voz kechishga va jamoat transportini tanlashga ikkilanishadi. Ular ko'pincha avtobuslar, tramvaylar va poezdlarni boshqalar uchun muqobil variantlar deb bilib, eshikdan eshikkacha haydash qulayligini afzal ko'rishadi. Natijada, yo'llarimiz tez-tez tiqilib qoladi.

Tabiiyki, mashina qo'yish joyini topish qiyinchilik tug'dirishi mumkin. Ba'zi kompaniyalar o'z xodimlari uchun avtoturargohlar tashkil qilsa-da, ko'pchilik odamlar ko'pincha ko'p qavatli bo'lgan jamoat avtoturargohlariga tayanishi yoki ko'chada to'xtashga urinishi kerak. Ko'pincha qattiq cheklovlar va to'xtash hisoblagichlarining ko'pligi tufayli joy topish ko'plab haydovchilar uchun asabiylashish manbaiga aylanadi. Bu holat ko'pincha stress va behuda vaqt sarflashga olib keladi.

Qonunga itoatkor fuqarolar ba'zan yo'l harakati qoidalariga kelganda erkinlikka yo'l qo'yishadi. Ular "TO'XTAGA MUMLKIN EMAS" belgilariga yoki to'xtash cheklovlarini ko'rsatuvchi chiziqlarga e'tibor bermasligi mumkin. Agar ular to'xtash hisoblagichidagi vaqt limitidan oshib ketgan taqdirda ham, ular xavotirlanmasligi mumkin - to ular old oynasida jarima qog'ozini topib, jarima to'lash kerakligini anglamaguncha. Bu xatti-harakat qulaylik muhim bo'lganda qoidalarni buzish vasvasasini ko'rsatadi.

Bunga javoban, ko'plab shaharlardagi hokimiyatlar shahar markazlarida avtomobillardan foydalanishni kamaytirishga harakat qilmoqda. Ular katta hududlarni piyodalar hududiga aylantirdilar va park-and-ride sxemalarini joriy qildilar, odamlarni o'z mashinalarini shahar chekkasida qoldirib, sayohatlarini avtobusda yakunlashga undadilar. Bu choralar eng tirband hududlarda transport hajmini kamaytirishga qaratilgan.

Ushbu sa'y-harakatlarga qaramay, tirbandlik darajasining oshishi shaharlarda, ayniqsa, tirbandlik soatlarida to'liq to'xtashlarga olib kelishi mumkin degan xavotirlar mavjud. Ko'plab yo'llarda tez-tez uzilishlar va tor joylar bo'lgani sababli, haydash endi yoqimli tajriba emas. Bu savolni tug'diradi: nega ko'pchiligimiz bu noqulayliklarga duch kelganimizda ham o'z mashinalarimizdan foydalanishda davom etamiz? Ehtimol, shaxsiy transport vositalariga bo'lgan ishonchimizni qayta ko'rib chiqishimiz va transportning muqobil turlarini o'rganishimiz kerakdir.

Hozirgi hukumatlar duch kelayotgan ko'p qirrali muammolar tobora transmilliy xususiyatga ega bo'lib bormoqda. Masalan, tirbandlikning keng tarqalgan muammosini olaylik. Dunyo bo'ylab deyarli barcha yirik shahar markazlari transport vositalarining ko'payishini va ular yo'l tarmoqlarini bo'g'ib qo'yadigan tirbandlikni boshqarish uchun samarali strategiyalarni ishlab chiqish zarurati bilan kurashmoqda.

Shaharlarimizni bosib olgan transport vositalarining katta qismi, shubhasiz, shaxsiy avtomobillardir. Haydovchilar, doimiy tirbandliklar bo'lishiga qaramay, shaxsiy transport vositalarining qulayligi va konforidan voz kechib, jamoat transportiga o'tishni xohlamaydilar. Ular ko'pincha avtobus, tramvay va poezdlarni boshqalar uchun muqobil transport vositasi sifatida ajratadilar, shu bilan birga shaxsiy avtomobilga egalik qilishning qulayligini talab qiladilar. Bu o'rnashib qolgan munosabat yo'llarimizning to'lib ketishiga sezilarli hissa qo'shadi.

Albatta, avtoturargohning mavjudligi har doim ham kafolatlanmaydi. Ba'zi tashkilotlar o'z xodimlarining hech bo'lmaganda bir qismini joylashtirish uchun avtoturargohlar yoki garajlar bilan ta'minlasa-da, ko'pchilik odamlar ko'pincha ko'p qavatli inshootlar bo'lgan jamoat avtoturargohlariga yoki ko'chada to'xtashga urinishga majbur bo'ladilar. Qat'iy qoidalarning keng tarqalganligini hisobga olsak, ko'pincha parkometrlar bilan ifodalanadi, to'xtash joyini topish ko'plab haydovchilar uchun g'azablanish manbai hisoblanadi. Avtoturargoh taqchilligi umidsizlik va noqonuniy to'xtashga olib keladi.

Odatda qonuniy va axloqiy me'yorlarga rioya qiladigan shaxslar ba'zan yo'l harakati qoidalarini chetlab o'tishga moyil bo'ladilar. Natijada, ular "TO'XTASH TAQIQLANGAN" belgilariga yoki to'xtash cheklovlarini belgilaydigan yo'l chiziqlariga e'tibor bermasliklari mumkin. Agar ularning transport vositasidan uzoqda bo'lishi parkometr tomonidan belgilangan vaqtdan oshsa, ular xavotirlanmaydilar - hech bo'lmaganda ularning old oynasiga yopishtirilgan jarima talonining yoqimsiz ko'rinishi ularni hayratga solmaguncha, jarima solinishini anglashga majbur qiladi. Bu shahar haydovchilari uchun keng tarqalgan vaziyatdir.

Shaharlar soni ortib borayotgan holda, hokimiyat organlari shahar markazlariga transport vositalarining kirishini qisqartirish choralarini faol ravishda ko'rmoqda. Shu maqsadda ular keng piyodalar zonalarini tashkil etish va shahar chetida mashinalarini qoldirib, sayohatlarini jamoat transportida yakunlashga odamlarni rag'batlantirish maqsadida park-and-ride tashabbuslarini joriy etdi. Bularning barchasi tirbandlikni kamaytirishga urinishlardir.

Shunga qaramay, transport hajmining tinimsiz oshishi oxir-oqibat shahar hududlarida, ayniqsa, eng gavjum soatlarda tirbandlikka olib kelishi haqida doimiy xavotirlar mavjud. Ko'plab yo'llarda tirbandlik va to'siqlar keng tarqalganligi sababli, haydash yoqimli tajribadan umidsizlikka aylandi. Shundan so'ng savol tug'iladi: nima uchun ko'pchiligimiz ushbu aniq kamchiliklarga qaramay, mashinalarimizdan foydalanishni davom ettiramiz?
